findings.title: get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime, so every non-empty optimized page raises TypeError
findings.description: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.ceil(value)` / `math.floor(value)`. `self.key` is `"datetime"` (set from `"-datetime"` in `BasePaginator.__init__`), and `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField` (`src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69`). `math.ceil(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key on `results[0]` when there is no cursor value (`src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122`) and on `results[-1]` (`cursors.py:137`). So a superuser or global-access member who sends `optimized_pagination=true` gets a 500 on any page that has rows. `DateTimePaginator` avoids this by converting to epoch milliseconds (`paginator.py:233-236`). No test covers this path.

findings.title: Unguarded `member.has_global_access` breaks the default path for org-token callers
findings.description:
`enable_advanced` is computed on every request, before `use_optimized` is checked. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (`src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346`), and `get_organization_by_id` leaves it `None` when there is no `user_id` (`src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/impl.py:123-141`). `convert_args` passes `user_id=request.user.id` (`src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:285-286`), so `member` is `None` for token callers. The default authentication includes `OrgAuthTokenAuthentication` (`src/sentry/api/base.py:87-92`). `OrganizationPermission.has_permission` accepts org tokens with `org:write` (`src/sentry/api/permissions.py:106-121`), which is this endpoint's GET scope. For those callers `request.user.is_superuser` is False, so `None.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`. A request that previously reached the normal query path now returns a 500. Fix: move the check inside the `use_optimized` branch and guard against `member is None`.

I did not open `OrgAuthTokenAuthentication.authenticate` to confirm its return value. The conclusion needs only that `request.user.id` is readable, which `convert_args` already requires.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets on the advanced branch are passed straight to the ORM slice and crash
findings.description: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]`. Cursor offsets come from the client, and `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative integers (`src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:58-59`). Django's QuerySet rejects negative slice starts ("Negative indexing is not supported."). I could not inspect the installed Django source in this sandbox, so this rests on Django's documented behavior. The comment at 878-879 says "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", which is wrong. The comment "permissions are checked at the queryset level" (879) is also wrong. The permission check is at the endpoint (`OrganizationAuditPermission`), and the queryset is only filtered by `organization_id`. This branch also skips the negative-offset rejection that `OffsetPaginator` applies (`paginator.py:286-287`).

findings.title: Negative next-cursor offsets are now silently clamped in the shared BasePaginator
findings.description: Before this change, `queryset[offset:stop]` with a negative offset raised. Now `start_offset = max(0, offset)` for next cursors, so the same request returns rows from the cursor position with no error. `BasePaginator.get_result` is the base for `DateTimePaginator`, `Paginator`, and other paginators, so this changes behavior for every endpoint that uses them, not only audit logs. The comment at 179-181 ("allow negative offsets") describes the opposite of what the clamp does. Prev-cursor negatives still reach the slice unchanged. Revert this hunk unless a stated requirement needs it.

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns the raw epoch-ms integer instead of a datetime
findings.description: `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` converts the cursor's epoch-ms value into an aware datetime (`paginator.py:238-241`). This class returns `cursor.value` unchanged, so `build_queryset` binds an integer against `auditlogentry.datetime` (`paginator.py:119-126`). The database will reject that comparison or compare the wrong values. The `get_item_key` crash currently stops this paginator from producing its own cursors, which hides this bug. Fixing the first finding would expose it.

findings.title: Role-gated, unvalidated offset bypasses a guard that other paginators apply
findings.description: Behavior changes based on `is_superuser` or `has_global_access`, and the client-supplied cursor offset is used without validation. Organization scoping (`organization_id=organization.id`, line 48) still holds, so this diff does not by itself leak cross-organization data. But the branch is meant to read "beyond normal pagination bounds", and it skips the negative-offset rejection that `OffsetPaginator` applies (`paginator.py:286-287`). The branch is undocumented and its justification is wrong. Either remove it or validate `cursor.offset >= 0` on every path.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result and is not actually optimized
findings.description: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (845-911) is a near-copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` (136-215) that differs in one branch. Its `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor` match `Paginator` for ints and `DateTimePaginator` for datetimes, but match neither exactly. A hook on the base class (for example, an overridable start-offset method) would express the one real difference. The name "Optimized" describes nothing the class does.

findings.title: Comments and docstrings claim performance and safety that the code does not implement
findings.description: The class docstring lists "Streamlined boundary condition handling" and "Optimized query path for large datasets". The query path is the same as `BasePaginator`, and no boundary handling was added. The `Cursor` comment (`src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27`) says it allows negative offsets, but no `Cursor` behavior changed. The endpoint comments at `organization_auditlogs.py:68-69` and `74-75` claim "performance optimization" and "high-performance" navigation, and nothing in the diff changes performance. Remove the claims or make them true.

findings.title: No tests cover the new parameter, role gate, paginator, or BasePaginator change
findings.description: A grep finds no reference to `optimized_pagination` or `OptimizedCursorPaginator` in the test suite. `tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py` has no test for a negative next-cursor offset. A single admin request with `optimized_pagination=true` and one audit-log row would have caught the `TypeError` in the first finding. Add tests for the default path, the optimized path with rows, a prev cursor, and a negative offset.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace and extra blank lines
findings.description: Trailing whitespace is on `organization_auditlogs.py:72` and `:89`, and on `paginator.py:824`, `:827`, and `:829`. Three blank lines precede `class OptimizedCursorPaginator` (`paginator.py:818-820`). Standard Python formatters (black, ruff) flag these. Run the formatter.
